definitions.explanation: Introductory statements made before getting to the main point.

examples.english: I'll say it without any preface.

examples.japanese: {前置|まえお}き⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{本題|ほんだい}→本題：12877_hondai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}って→入る：00494_hairu⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Skip the preamble and get to the main point.

examples.japanese: {前置|まえお}き⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{長|なが}く→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦なりました→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{本題|ほんだい}→本題：12877_hondai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{移|うつ}ります→移る：01232_utsuru⟧。
examples.english: The preamble got long, but let me move to the main topic.

notes:
{前置|まえお}き refers to introductory remarks made before the main point. Often used when someone takes too long to get to the point, or when the speaker wants to signal they are skipping straight to what matters.

ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧ (before) + ⟦{置|お}き→置く：01092_oku⟧ (placing) — literally "placing something before" the main topic.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {前置|まえお}き⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{長|なが}い→長い：00491_nagai⟧: the preamble is long (often a complaint)
- {前置|まえお}きなし⟦で→で：00502_de⟧: without any preface, getting straight to the point
- {前置|まえお}き⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧: skip the preamble (impatient)
- {前置|まえお}き⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧さておき: setting the preamble aside

USAGE:
Often used self-referentially: {前置|まえお}き⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{長|なが}く→長い：00491_nagai⟧⟦なりました→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧... ("my preamble has gotten long, but...") is a polite way to transition to the main topic.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{本題|ほんだい}→本題：12877_hondai⟧: main topic (what comes after the {前置|まえお}き)
- ⟦{序文|じょぶん}→序文：06205_jobun⟧: preface (in written works)
- ⟦{導入|どうにゅう}→導入：10127_dounyuu⟧: introduction (more formal/general)
